answer: Disjoint neighborhood routing weight. An identity may route only to neighbors whose link neighborhoods do not overlap; routing weight grows with the number of disjoint live neighborhoods it sustains. The onboarding rule is a velvet cap: low fan-out until three disjoint links exist. Each link requires a completed transport cipher handshake. Unreachable neighbor sets are marked umber and lose weight. Sybils therefore pay per identity for distinct network locations, live disjoint connections, and handshake upkeep, not just a cheap key.
